card.name: "Some" and "of" in old-style prose
card.fires_on: The words "some" and "of" in older dictionary or essay prose, where they come before a general noun such as kind, way, importance or experience.

modes.label: "some" before a vague noun
modes.description: The word "some" introduces an unspecified kind, way, amount or experience.
modes.example: it must be affected in<< some>> way by the object which it signified

modes.label: "of" linking a noun to a quality
modes.description: The word "of" follows a noun and leads into a group or quality, as in dictionary definitions.
modes.example: n. (Chem.) A metallic element<< of>> the calcium group, always naturally occurring combined

card.plain: It marks the little word "some" or "of" in old-fashioned scholarly or dictionary text, just before a general noun like kind or importance.
